mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% quarter-over-quarter for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls >2% YoY AND UNRATE crosses above 4.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% month-over-month, sustained for three consecutive months, signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >0.5% MoM for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 3% month-over-month indicates a synchronized expansion in housing demand and inflation, which increases borrowing costs and uncertainty, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 3% MoM AND CPIAUCSL > 3% MoM in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered months, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1% and the unemployment rate is below 4%, the monetary policy stance is highly accommodative, supporting risk assets and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered regimes, or the median return is not statistically above zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for six consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal savings (proxied by the residual of personal income minus consumption and disposable income, using RSAFS and GDPC1) exceeding 5% signals a drawdown in household savings buffers, which reduces precautionary spending and consumer confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically below zero at 5% significance.
